That draw is the next caller handoff, not the missing source owner: js/unported_monster_actions.js:assertSimpleActionState rejects the pet solely for mleashed && pet !== usteed before its normal action.

C input history: wish an uncursed leash, create a tame little dog, apply it at step 41. The C message is You slip the leash around your little dog. At step 47 hero is (36,5), pet (37,6). First h at 48 moves hero to (35,5) and pet to (36,5). Subsequent h inputs reach hero/pet coordinates (34,5)/(34,6), (33,5)/(34,5), (32,5)/(32,6). .cache/v27-leash-tame-dog/c-frames.json stores decoded C screen evidence.

C dog_goal:504–508 sets APPORT and hero coordinates for leashed pets; dog_move:1092–1094 rejects candidates with distu > 4, 1199–1202 whimpers at traps regardless of usual avoidance, 1237 and 1246 skip the normal curse/backtrack draws, and 1254–1257 owns the remaining candidate RNG. Recording step 49 first reaches rn2(1)=0 at dog_move:1255; step 51 reaches its rn2(12) arm. Existing JS contains these branches, so removing the planner guard alone is not evidence that the whole owner is complete.

Whole dog_move:1276–1356 also releases the leash before an ALLOW_U attack and handles stationary/eating pets farther than squared distance 4. Its newdogpos arm preserves the unusual raw dirtocoord/goodpos sequence, tests m_in_out_region using nix/niy, then removes/places the pet, newsym and set_apparxy in C order. js/dogmove.js delegates this to repositionLeashedPet (1345 and 1698), but the production adapter has no such operation. The selected short case establishes normal leashed following; it does not prove this forced repositioning arm.

Additional source gap: apply.c:check_leash:931–994 is called before final map restoration in hack.c:domove_core:2962, but JS domove_core currently omits that call. The allmain teleport and trap teleport callers retain mislabeled dog.c check_leash notes. This is a separate source-owned void dependency; retain an explicit named gap or reserve/port whole check_leash and its required return dependencies. Do not invent pull/choke/snapping effects as part of the dog_move candidate loop.

Actionable scope: reserve whole source:dogmove.c:dog_move and contract:leashed-pet-movement, plus the bounded source:monmove.c:m_move/planner adapter caller if required. Primary paths js/dogmove.js, js/unported_monster_actions.js, affected scripts/dogmove*.test.mjs and scripts/unported-monster-actions.test.mjs, recipes/dogmove.c and recordings/dogmove.c. Independent validation needs source-pinned tests for source distance thresholds and direction fallback order; clone preflight versus live state/RNG/output tests; an independently chosen leash-following recipe and cheap pet/role variation; a blocked-layout or eating/trapped-pet variation that actually reaches newdogpos repositioning. If m_unleash/check_leash are added, separate active caller evidence is required for death/untaming, snapping/cursed-choking and teleport. The admitted step 48–55 range covers only ordinary following, not sleeping pets, hunger, displacement, Conflict/minions, forced drag, death or teleport.

Ownership limit: B136 owns artifact intrinsic and see_monsters plus restore display contracts; C134 owns setuwep/forced primary drop. Neither currently reserves dog_move or leashed movement, but their pending broad adapter/caller deliveries must be merged at a clean boundary before source wiring is finalized. Existing tests deliberately require the ordinary leashed-pet refusal and must change only when the owner/caller behavior is implemented.
